Parallel Activations Drift Detector (PADD)

Source: R/dfr_padd.R
dfr_padd.Rd

Unsupervised batch drift detector of Komorniczak and Ksieniewicz (2024). The data stream is processed in chunks of chunk_size observations, each passed through a randomly initialised, never trained neural network (one hidden ReLU layer of hidden units, outputs ReLU outputs and a softmax, weights drawn from N(0, 0.1)). For every output, replications Student t-tests compare a sample of sample_size activations of the current chunk with a sample of the activations stored since the last drift (both drawn with replacement). A drift is reported when more than threshold * outputs * replications tests are significant at level alpha; the stored activations are then cleared. Since it monitors the inputs only, it is used for virtual concept drift.

Usage

dfr_padd(
  target_feat = NULL,
  chunk_size = 200,
  alpha = 0.05,
  threshold = 0.17,
  outputs = 30,
  replications = 35,
  sample_size = 75,
  hidden = 10,
  seed = NULL,
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the columns to be monitored. NULL (the default) monitors every numeric column.

chunk_size

Number of observations of a chunk (the batches of the paper, 200 in its experiments).

alpha

Significance level of the t-tests.

threshold

Fraction of significant tests above which a drift is reported.

outputs

Number of outputs of the network (e).

replications

Number of t-tests per output (r).

sample_size

Size of the samples drawn for every test (s).

hidden

Number of units of the hidden layer.

seed

Seed of the network weights and of the samples. NULL draws it from the global generator when the detector is created; the global random state is left unchanged.

weights

Optional fixed network: a list with the hidden layer ((n_features + 1) x hidden, the last row is the bias) and the output layer (hidden x outputs). By default it is drawn on the first chunk.

Value

dfr_padd object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, on the last observation of every chunk, the fraction of significant tests (significant), and obj$weights the network.

Details

The defaults are those of the reference implementation (https://github.com/w4k2/padd, methods.py). The paper's experiments use outputs = 12, replications = 12, sample_size = 50, and alpha = 0.07, threshold = 0.19 for sudden drifts or alpha = 0.13, threshold = 0.26 for gradual ones.

As in the reference, the first chunk is only stored; after a drift the stored activations are replaced by those of the drifting chunk; the t-test is the pooled-variance (Student) test, and a test whose two samples are constant (undefined p-value) is not significant. The drift is reported on the last observation of the chunk. Rows with missing values are dropped. reset_state() clears the stored activations and keeps the network.

References

Komorniczak, J. and Ksieniewicz, P. (2024). Unsupervised concept drift detection based on parallel activations of neural network. arXiv:2404.07776.

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
# 12 chunks of 200 observations; the mean of 3 of the 10 features moves at chunk 7.
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(2400 * 10), ncol = 10)
x[1201:2400, 1:3] <- x[1201:2400, 1:3] + 1
detector <- dfr_padd(outputs = 12, replications = 12, sample_size = 50,
                     alpha = 0.07, threshold = 0.19, seed = 1)
model <- fit(detector, as.data.frame(x))
which(!is.na(model$drifter_output$significant) & model$drifter_output$significant > 0.19)
#> [1] 1400
